messages.subject: Computing a variable once
parts:
Hello,

In the following code, the call to messages() is costly. How would I call it once and remove the need to call it twice in
output$qplot and output$summary?

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  messages <- reactive({
    s <- getdata (build      = input$build
                  ,quantity  = fixup(input$what)
                  ,product   = input$product
                  ,channel   = input$channel
                  ,version   = input$version
                  ,os        = input$os
                  ,osversion = input$osversion
                  ,reasons   = input$reasons
                  ,arch      = input$arch)
    s <- as.data.frame(s)
    if(nrow(s)==0) NULL else s
  })

  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    m <- messages()
    summary(m$s)
  })
 
 
  output$qplot <- renderPlot({
    m <- messages()
    if(nrow(m)>0){
      library(lattice)
      x <- m[,1];ps <- m[,2]
      print( xyplot( log(x+1) ~ ps, ylab=sprintf('log of %s',input$what),xlab='Quantile',col='black'
                  ,main=sprintf('Quantile Plot of Log of %s',input$what)
                  ,aspect=1,type='p',panel=function(x,y,...){
                    panel.grid()
                    panel.xyplot(x,y,...)
                    panel.loess(x,y,col='red',lwd=2)
                  }))
    }
  })
})

Thanks
Saptarshi

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Computing a variable once
parts:
Saptarshi -

It should only run messages() once when an input value changes. You can check this by inserting a print() statement in messages() and seeing how many times it prints out the value. I know it looks like it will be run twice, but Shiny does work to make sure it's only run once. It caches the value and simply hands it out, until an input value changes.

This page (and the next two) in the tutorial explains it in more depth:
http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview

-Winston
